definitions.gloss: proselytizing; missionary work; spreading a religion
definitions.explanation: The act of spreading religious teachings and trying to convert people to a particular faith.
Informally used to describe passionately recommending a hobby, product, or interest to others, trying to win them over. Common in internet and otaku culture.

examples.japanese: {宣教師|せんきょうし}が{日本|にほん}で{布教|ふきょう}{活動|かつどう}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: Missionaries carried out evangelization activities in Japan.

examples.japanese: キリスト{教|きょう}の{布教|ふきょう}は{戦国時代|せんごくじだい}に{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The spread of Christianity began in the Warring States period.

examples.japanese: {江戸幕府|えどばくふ}はキリスト{教|きょう}の{布教|ふきょう}を{禁止|きんし}し、{厳|きび}しく{取|と}り{締|し}まった。
examples.english: The Edo shogunate banned Christian proselytizing and cracked down on it severely.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}に{好|す}きなバンドを{布教|ふきょう}した。
examples.english: I evangelized my favorite band to my friends.

examples.japanese: このアニメ、{絶対|ぜったい}おもしろいから{布教|ふきょう}させて。
examples.english: This anime is definitely great—let me convert you.

examples.japanese: SNSで{自分|じぶん}の{推|お}しを{布教|ふきょう}するファンが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many fans use social media to promote their favorite idol.

notes:
USAGE:
{布教|ふきょう} is a compound of {布|ふ} (to spread) and {教|きょう} (teaching). Originally a religious term, it has been adopted in informal Japanese to mean enthusiastically recommending something to others.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {布教|ふきょう}{活動|かつどう} (missionary activities)
- {布教|ふきょう}する (to proselytize; to promote enthusiastically)
- {推|お}しを{布教|ふきょう}する (to promote one's favorite idol/character)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {布教|ふきょう}: spreading a faith or interest (original: religious; extended: hobby/fandom)
- {伝道|でんどう}: evangelism, preaching (specifically Christian)
- {宣教|せんきょう}: missionary work (formal, institutional)
